validation_note: Every case in this batch is supported by an official government, UN, World Bank or public institutional source. Analogies are management lessons, not automatic diagnoses for Olszówka/Gardeja.

cases.name: Lake Titicaca — Puno basin
cases.observed_pattern: The World Bank reports that Lake Titicaca faces significant threats from untreated wastewater, water shortages and drought. A 2025 program targets new wastewater treatment plants, expanded sanitation, water reuse and climate-resilient water services in Puno.
cases.management_lesson: Water quantity and quality must be tracked together. A basin can lose usable water before it loses visible surface area, so sanitation, reuse and drought indicators belong in the same management system.

provenance.title: Peru to Advance Wastewater Management and Circular Economy strategies with $200 Million World Bank Program
provenance.supports: Lake Titicaca is threatened by untreated wastewater, water shortages and drought; the Puno program includes wastewater treatment, sanitation expansion, reuse and climate-resilient water infrastructure.

cases.name: Lake Winnipeg
cases.observed_pattern: Environment and Climate Change Canada reports long-term water-quality deterioration driven mainly by excess nutrients and other pollutants across the large basin. Human sources include municipal and industrial wastewater, agricultural runoff and land-development or wetland losses; excess nutrients contribute to larger and more frequent algal blooms.
cases.management_lesson: A lake problem may originate far upstream. Tributary loads, wetland buffering and source-specific nutrient reductions should be measured rather than relying only on samples taken inside the lake.

provenance.publisher: Environment and Climate Change Canada / Canada Water Agency
provenance.title: Reductions in phosphorus loads to Lake Winnipeg
provenance.supports: Excess phosphorus degrades Lake Winnipeg water quality; funded projects reduce phosphorus entering rivers and streams that flow into the lake.

provenance.title: Nutrients in Lake Winnipeg
provenance.supports: Municipal and industrial wastewater, agricultural runoff, atmospheric pollution and wetland or land-use change contribute nutrients that drive algal blooms in Lake Winnipeg.

cases.name: Lake Okeechobee
cases.observed_pattern: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers approved deviations from the Lake Okeechobee Regulation Schedule to reduce harmful-algal-bloom risk by holding releases when blooms are prevalent and releasing more water when conditions are more favorable. USACE field work also showed that untreated surrounding water can reintroduce bloom material through water exchange.
cases.management_lesson: Flow timing can change water-quality risk even without changing annual volume. A management model should couple water level, bloom state, exchange pathways and release timing instead of optimizing one variable alone.

provenance.publisher: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District
provenance.title: Corps announces approval of a planned deviation from Lake O Regulation Schedule to reduce risk from Harmful Algal Blooms
provenance.supports: USACE altered the operating schedule to reduce HAB risk by changing the timing of releases while maintaining other project purposes.

provenance.publisher: U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center
provenance.title: Field Demonstration of a Peroxide-Based Algaecide for Harmful Algal Bloom Control in Lake Okeechobee
provenance.supports: Bloom control was less effective where surrounding bloom-affected water re-entered the treatment area through water-exchange processes.

cases.name: Murray–Darling Basin — environmental connectivity
cases.observed_pattern: The Murray–Darling Basin Authority identifies longitudinal surface-water connectivity to and through Menindee Lakes as a management objective and maintains a basin-wide environmental watering strategy to improve ecological condition across connected river and wetland sites.
cases.management_lesson: Connectivity is measurable infrastructure for ecosystems. Management should track whether water can move between refuges, channels and wetlands at the right time, not merely whether isolated pools contain water.

provenance.title: Stocktake and options for improving connectivity in the northern Murray–Darling Basin
provenance.supports: The report analyzes actions intended to improve longitudinal surface-water connectivity across the northern Basin to and through Menindee Lakes.

provenance.title: 2025 Basin-wide environmental watering strategy
provenance.supports: The strategy guides long-term environmental watering and reports improved environmental condition at sites managed under the strategy.

cases.name: Mekong Delta
cases.observed_pattern: The World Bank reports that the Mekong Delta is sinking, with excessive groundwater extraction, sand mining and reduced sediment deposition among the causes. Reduced dry-season river flow accelerates salinity intrusion, while upstream dams and intensive water-control infrastructure alter flows, sediment movement and ecological connectivity.
cases.management_lesson: Groundwater, sediment and surface flow form one coupled system. Monitoring should combine land elevation, pumping, salinity fronts, river discharge and floodplain storage because solving one component can shift risk elsewhere.

provenance.title: How is Vietnam’s Mekong Delta adapting to a changing climate?
provenance.supports: The Delta is subsiding due to excessive groundwater extraction, sand mining and reduced sediment deposition; reduced dry-season flow worsens salinity intrusion.

provenance.title: A Tale of Two Shrimpers: How will the Mekong Delta adapt to climate change?
provenance.supports: Wetland drainage and water-control infrastructure disrupted ecological connectivity and sediment/nutrient flows; the project emphasizes monitoring and integrated planning.

cases.name: Laguna de Bay
cases.observed_pattern: The World Bank reports severe pollution in Laguna de Bay from industrial, commercial, agricultural and domestic sources. Waste and untreated discharges also clog tributaries and canals and can exacerbate flooding. Restoration programs combine wastewater treatment, solid-waste control, drainage, flood measures and local watershed governance.
cases.management_lesson: Water quality, channel capacity and flood risk can share the same upstream causes. Source control and tributary maintenance should be linked rather than managed by separate dashboards.

provenance.title: Philippines: Small Towns Find Solutions In Their Backyards to Fight Pollution
provenance.supports: Laguna Lake receives industrial, commercial, agricultural and domestic pollution; local projects address solid waste, wastewater, erosion and flood prevention.

provenance.title: Philippines: Over 13 Million People to Benefit from World Bank Support to Cleanup Laguna de Bay through Local Government Units
provenance.supports: The program funds wastewater, solid-waste, drainage and flood-control work along the river systems draining into Laguna de Bay.

cases.name: Lake Qaraoun / Litani River
cases.observed_pattern: The World Bank identifies untreated municipal and industrial wastewater, solid waste, fertilizers and pesticides as major pollution sources in the Litani–Qaraoun system. It also reports declining water availability from drought while demand grew, making quality and quantity pressures concurrent.
cases.management_lesson: A shrinking usable-water supply may be caused simultaneously by pollution and hydrologic shortage. Management should calculate both physical volume and the fraction of that volume that remains safe or usable.

provenance.title: Lebanon Takes a Step in Addressing Water Pollution
provenance.supports: The Litani River and Qaraoun Lake are heavily polluted by untreated wastewater, solid waste and agricultural chemicals while drought reduces available water.

provenance.title: Lebanon - Lake Qaraoun Pollution Prevention Project
provenance.supports: The project reduces untreated sewage to the Litani, connects sewerage to treatment plants, reduces fertilizer/pesticide use and removes riverbank waste.

cases.name: Dianchi Lake
cases.observed_pattern: The World Bank reports that Dianchi Lake deteriorated from Grade II water quality in the 1980s to the lowest Grade V by the mid-2000s as population growth and pollution increased. An integrated program expanded wastewater and solid-waste services, river improvements and monitoring, including a data-sharing platform for lake-basin agencies.
cases.management_lesson: Restoration benefits from a common basin data platform. Pollution sources, treatment capacity and monitoring records should be shared across agencies so management responds to the same evidence base.

provenance.title: Transforming China’s Yunnan Province: Better Water Infrastructure for a Sustainable Future
provenance.supports: Dianchi water quality declined severely; the response combined wastewater, solid-waste and river improvements with integrated basin management, monitoring and inter-agency data sharing.

cases.name: Lake Ohrid
cases.observed_pattern: UNESCO identifies inadequate wastewater and solid-waste treatment, urban development and nutrient growth as serious threats to Lake Ohrid's oligotrophic ecology. Current monitoring has detected organic and fecal pollution hotspots and tracks nutrients associated with eutrophication and green-algae growth.
cases.management_lesson: For naturally low-nutrient lakes, small nutrient increases can be ecologically important before obvious physical shrinkage occurs. Baseline ecology and local pollution hotspots therefore matter as much as lake area.

provenance.title: Natural and Cultural Heritage of the Ohrid region
provenance.supports: UNESCO lists inadequate wastewater and solid-waste treatment, urban development and increasing nutrients as threats to the lake's oligotrophic ecology.

provenance.title: Decision 47 COM 7B.54 — Natural and Cultural Heritage of the Ohrid region
provenance.supports: The Committee notes wastewater upgrades and monitoring but calls for urgent action on pollution hotspots and eutrophication pressures.

cases.name: Uru Uru Lake
cases.observed_pattern: The Convention on Wetlands documents threats to Uru Uru Lake from mining activities, plastic pollution and climate change. Community restoration uses nature-based solutions including floating structures made from recovered materials and native totora plants.
cases.management_lesson: Local ecological restoration can be useful when it targets a demonstrated pressure and is monitored, but it does not replace basin-scale pollution control. Community observations can also provide an early-warning layer alongside satellite data.

provenance.title: Dayana Blanco Quiroga, Bolivia
provenance.supports: Ramsar describes mining, plastic pollution and climate change as threats to Uru Uru Lake and documents community restoration using nature-based solutions and native aquatic plants.
